items.title: High-yield spread 3.63% and investment-grade 0.97% on Nov. 23
items.subtitle: ICE BofA U.S. high-yield and corporate option-adjusted spreads, daily
items.take: FRED shows the ICE BofA high-yield option-adjusted spread at 3.63% on Nov. 23, down from 3.76% on Nov. 20 but above 3.23% on Nov. 13. The investment-grade spread was 0.97% on Nov. 23, versus 0.98% on Nov. 20 and 0.89% on Nov. 13. The gap between the two was 2.66 percentage points on Nov. 23. AlphaGen read: both spreads are wider than on Nov. 13, and high yield has moved by more.
items.source: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.title: 10-year real yield 2.77% and breakeven 2.15% on Nov. 20 (breakeven 2.13% on Nov. 23)
items.subtitle: 10-year TIPS real yield and 10-year breakeven inflation rate, daily
items.take: FRED shows the 10-year real yield at 2.77% on Nov. 20, down from 2.92% on Nov. 16, and the 10-year breakeven inflation rate at 2.15% on Nov. 20 and 2.13% on Nov. 23, versus 2.20% on Nov. 16. The two components together make up the nominal 10-year yield, which was 4.92% on Nov. 20. AlphaGen read: over Nov. 16-20 the decline was mostly in the real component.
items.source: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.title: Euro at $1.1034 on Nov. 13, the lowest of the past year, as the broad dollar index hit 122.65
items.subtitle: USD per euro and broad dollar index, daily
items.take: FRED shows the euro at $1.1034 on Nov. 13, down from $1.1235 on Nov. 5 and from the year's high of $1.1980 on Jan. 27. The Federal Reserve's broad dollar index stood at 122.65 on Nov. 13, the highest in a year of daily readings, versus a low of 117.44 on Jan. 29. AlphaGen read: the two series point the same way, a firmer dollar through the first half of November.
items.source: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.title: Rates: 3-month 4.34%, 2-year 4.80%, 10-year 5.07% on Nov. 18
items.subtitle: Treasury yields, percent, daily
items.take: FRED shows the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.07% on Nov. 18, down from 5.15% on Nov. 13, while the 2-year was 4.80% and the 3-month 4.34%. On Nov. 10 the three read 4.98%, 4.73% and 4.30%. AlphaGen read: the 10-year's lead over the 3-month bill was 0.73 percentage point on Nov. 18 and the 2-year's was 0.46 (AlphaGen calculations).

items.title: Oil: Brent $92.94, WTI $89.53 on Nov. 17
items.subtitle: Crude oil spot prices, dollars per barrel, daily
items.take: FRED shows Brent at $92.94 per barrel on Nov. 17, up from $90.16 on Nov. 10 and below its $95.42 reading on Nov. 12. WTI was $89.53, leaving Brent $3.41 above it. AlphaGen read: the Brent-WTI gap widened from $0.54 on Nov. 10 to $3.41 on Nov. 17 (AlphaGen calculation).

items.title: Dollar-yen: 159.93 yen per dollar on Nov. 13
items.subtitle: Japanese yen per U.S. dollar, daily noon buying rates in New York
items.take: FRED shows 159.93 yen per dollar on Nov. 13, up from 157.76 on Nov. 5, a rise of 2.17 yen. The rate was higher at each reading from Nov. 9 (157.99) to Nov. 13. AlphaGen read: a higher number means a weaker yen against the dollar.

items.title: Treasury yields: 2-year 4.88%, 10-year 5.15%, 30-year 5.47%
items.subtitle: 2-, 10- and 30-year Treasury constant-maturity yields, daily, percent
items.take: FRED shows the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.88% on Nov. 13, up from 4.46% on Nov. 5, the 10-year at 5.15% from 4.84%, and the 30-year at 5.47% from 5.25%. The rises were 42, 31 and 22 basis points. The 30-year minus 2-year gap narrowed to 0.59 point from 0.79 (AlphaGen calculation). AlphaGen read: the curve flattened because shorter maturities rose the most.
items.source: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.title: The 10-year yield at 5.10%: 2.86 real, 2.24 breakeven
items.subtitle: 10-year Treasury constant-maturity yield, 10-year TIPS yield and 10-year breakeven inflation, daily, percent
items.take: FRED shows the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.10% on Nov. 12, up from 4.84% on Nov. 5. The 10-year TIPS (real) yield was 2.86% on Nov. 12, from 2.60% on Nov. 5, and the 10-year breakeven rate was 2.24%, from 2.24% on Nov. 5. The real yield plus breakeven equals the nominal yield (2.86 + 2.24 = 5.10). AlphaGen read: the whole week's rise came through the real yield.
items.source: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.title: High-yield credit spreads sit 2.40 points above investment grade
items.subtitle: ICE BofA US High Yield and US Corporate index option-adjusted spreads, daily, percent
items.take: FRED shows the ICE BofA US High Yield option-adjusted spread at 3.30% on Nov. 11, down from 3.48% on Nov. 5 and 3.40% on Nov. 3. The US Corporate (investment-grade) spread was 0.90% on Nov. 11, from 0.93% on Nov. 5. The gap between the two was 2.40 percentage points on Nov. 11. AlphaGen read: both spreads edged lower over the week, meaning the extra yield investors demand over Treasuries on corporate bonds narrowed slightly.
items.source: ICE Data Indices via FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.title: The 2-year Treasury yield sits 0.68 point above SOFR
items.subtitle: 2-year constant-maturity Treasury yield vs. the secured overnight financing rate, daily, percent
items.take: FRED shows the 2-year Treasury constant-maturity yield at 4.56% on Nov. 9, up from 4.46% on Nov. 5, while SOFR was 3.88% on Nov. 9, down from 3.95% on Nov. 2. The gap of 0.68 percentage point compares with 0.64 on Nov. 2 (4.59% against 3.95%). The Fed's federal funds target range was 3.75% to 4.00% on Nov. 11. AlphaGen read: a 2-year yield above overnight rates means the market yield on short Treasuries is currently higher than where policy rates stand.
items.source: U.S. Department of the Treasury and Federal Reserve Bank of New York via FRED

items.title: Jobless claims at 189,000: the lowest of the last six weekly readings
items.subtitle: Initial claims for unemployment insurance, seasonally adjusted, weekly, persons
items.take: Initial jobless claims were 189,000 for the week ended Oct. 31, down from 195,000 in each of the two prior weeks (Oct. 17 and Oct. 24) and 200,000 for the week ended Oct. 10. The Oct. 31 reading is the lowest of the six weekly observations from Sept. 26 on, which ranged from 189,000 to 200,000. BLS separately reported October payrolls up 165,000 and an unemployment rate of 4.1%. Low claims alongside modest payroll growth fits the low-hire, low-fire description Fed Governor Waller used on Nov. 10.
items.source: U.S. Employment and Training Administration via FRED

items.title: A 7.32% mortgage and a 5.13% 10-year: the housing rate gap
items.subtitle: Freddie Mac 30-year fixed mortgage average (weekly) and 10-year Treasury constant maturity yield (daily), percent
items.take: The 30-year fixed mortgage rate averaged 7.32% for the week ending October 22, down from 7.40% on October 15 and October 8, and up from 7.03% on September 24. The 10-year Treasury yield was 5.13% on October 21 versus 5.10% on October 15. On October 15 the mortgage rate was 2.30 percentage points above the 10-year yield (7.40% less 5.10%). Freddie Mac reported a year-ago average of 6.19%.
items.source: Freddie Mac PMMS and Federal Reserve H.15 via FRED

items.title: What's in a 5% 10-year yield: 2.77% real, 2.35% inflation compensation
items.subtitle: 10-year Treasury constant maturity yield, 10-year TIPS yield and 10-year breakeven inflation rate, daily, percent
items.take: The 10-year Treasury yield was 5.12% on October 20, down from 5.19% on October 14. The 10-year TIPS (real) yield was 2.77% on October 20 versus 2.84% on October 14, and the 10-year breakeven inflation rate was 2.35% on both dates. The 7 basis point decline in the nominal yield over those four sessions therefore came entirely from the real component, since 2.77% plus 2.35% equals 5.12%. Breakeven inflation holding steady while real yields set the level means the bond market's price for inflation is not what is driving long-term borrowing costs.
items.source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (H.15) via FRED (DGS10, DFII10, T10YIE)

items.title: The oil shock is a Brent shock: a $25 gap over WTI
items.subtitle: Brent (Europe) and WTI (Cushing, Okla.) crude oil spot prices, daily, dollars per barrel
items.take: Brent crude was $126.55 a barrel on October 14 and WTI was $101.91, a spread of $24.64. On October 8 the gap was $31.92, with Brent at $130.18 and WTI at $98.26, so the spread has narrowed by $7.28 in four trading sessions as WTI rose and Brent eased. Even after that narrowing, a premium of this size says the shock is concentrated in internationally traded, seaborne crude rather than U.S. inland supply. That matters for inflation abroad, where Brent-linked fuel costs bite hardest, and for U.S. refiners and exporters, which are buying crude far below the global benchmark.
items.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration via FRED (DCOILBRENTEU, DCOILWTICO)

items.title: Junk spreads are widening; investment grade is not
items.subtitle: ICE BofA US High Yield and US Corporate (IG) option-adjusted spreads, daily, %
items.take: The ICE BofA US High Yield option-adjusted spread stood at 3.16% on October 13, up 56 basis points from its 2026 low of 2.60% on August 28 and 33 basis points above its January 2 level of 2.83%. The investment-grade spread was 0.83%, only 4 basis points wider than on January 2. That divergence suggests investors are repricing risk in lower-rated, more energy- and consumer-sensitive borrowers rather than in credit broadly. With bank releases this week showing higher card-loss provisions, high-yield is the spread to watch for signs the oil shock is reaching corporate balance sheets.
items.source: ICE Data Indices via FRED (BAMLH0A0HYM2, BAMLC0A0CM)

items.title: From inverted to positive: the 2s10s Treasury curve
items.subtitle: 2-year and 10-year Treasury yields, daily, %
items.take: As of October 13, the 10-year Treasury yielded 5.21% and the 2-year 4.79%, a positive spread of 42 basis points on the Treasury's daily par curve. The chart shows how different that is from 2022 through 2024, when 2-year yields sat above 10-year yields for an extended stretch. A positive slope with both yields this high means lenders are demanding more to lend long, which feeds directly into mortgage, corporate, and federal borrowing costs.
